We propose a phased, multi-site delivery plan that maintains hospital operations, accelerates repeatable engineering across twelve locations, and targets overall completion within ~10–13 months from Notice to Proceed—anchored to our demonstrated solar delivery timelines (10 months and 13 months on completed solar deployments) [CAP-032][CAP-044]. The three-year O&M period will commence from site-wise commissioning as required, supported by our in-country 24–48h response model and quarterly preventive maintenance approach used on O&M contracts [CO-PROFILE].

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–6): Mobilization, HSE and access protocols for operational healthcare sites, stakeholder kickoff, and site surveys at all hospitals. We will run surveys in parallel teams to complete verified as-built data capture and load/space assessments quickly; we execute site safety plans on infrastructure deployments under a documented HSE policy [CO-PROFILE].

Phase 2 (Weeks 4–10): Detailed engineering design package per hospital (single-line diagrams, layout, structural checks, protection coordination) and compliance mapping to IEC 62548 and the Pakistan Electricity Code (to be enforced through our ISO 9001 quality management system) [CO-PROFILE].

Phase 3 (Weeks 8–24): Procurement and logistics of Tier‑1 PV modules, string inverters, and mounting structures (final makes/models at submittal). Our library does not yet evidence Tier‑1 module efficiency (21%) or 25‑year linear warranty documentation; we will meet this through OEM datasheets/warranties submitted for approval prior to ordering.

Phase 4 (Weeks 16–44): Civil/electrical installation in rolling waves (3–4 hospitals at a time), followed by testing, commissioning, and performance verification.

Phase 5 (Weeks 10–48, in parallel): Net-metering applications and DISCO coordination. Our library does not yet evidence prior net‑metering approvals; we will address this via an assigned approvals lead and early submission immediately after design freeze.

Phase 6 (Weeks 36–52): SCADA-based monitoring go-live with a central dashboard. Our library does not yet evidence SCADA delivery; we will deliver this through an OEM platform and integration support from our network design capability [CAP-045]. Training for hospital engineering staff will be conducted site-wise at commissioning and reinforced during early O&M [CO-PROFILE].
